question: Special provisions for certain states are covered under which Part of the Indian Constitution?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Part XXI**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Special provisions for certain states** in India are outlined under **Part XXI** of the Constitution, titled "Temporary, Transitional, and Special Provisions."
 
• This part of the Constitution primarily addresses the **unique conditions of certain states** and regions, allowing them to have special privileges and provisions due to their distinctive social, cultural, or geographical conditions.
 
• **Article 370** (now abrogated) provided special status to **Jammu & Kashmir**, granting it autonomy in various areas except defense, foreign affairs, finance, and communications. *Hence, this was part of Part XXI.*
 
• **Article 371** and its sub-clauses (Article 371-A to 371-J) provide **special provisions for states** like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, etc., focusing on administrative, cultural, and economic development. *Hence, this is covered under Part XXI.*
 
• These provisions ensure that the **rights and interests of the residents** in these states are safeguarded, considering their unique circumstances. *Hence, Part XXI applies to special provisions for certain states.*
 
• Part XXI reflects the **diverse nature of India** and acknowledges the need for flexible governance in states with distinct characteristics.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Special Provisions under Part XXI:**

 
 
• **Article 370**: Provided temporary provisions for Jammu & Kashmir, granting it autonomy in certain legislative areas. This article was abrogated in **August 2019**.
 
• **Article 371**: Contains special provisions for states like Maharashtra and Gujarat to ensure equitable distribution of resources and development.
 
• **Article 371-A**: Ensures the protection of the **customary laws** and social practices of Nagaland, as well as the religious and land-related rights of its people.
 
• **Article 371-B**: Provides special representation for the tribal areas of Assam in its legislature.
 
• **Article 371-J**: Grants special provisions for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region, ensuring reservation in employment and education.
 
 
 
• **Key Features of Part XXI:**
 
 
• Part XXI is unique to the Indian Constitution as it addresses **temporary, transitional, and special provisions**.
 
• It reflects India’s commitment to addressing the **diverse needs of its states** and regions, ensuring their protection and development.
 
• The provisions have helped integrate culturally, geographically, and administratively distinct states into the Indian Union.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Examples of Special Provisions:**

 
 
• **Nagaland (Article 371-A)**: Protects the cultural and religious practices of the Naga people, including their land ownership rights.
 
• **Assam (Article 371-B)**: Ensures political representation for tribal areas.
 
• **Andhra Pradesh (Article 371-D)**: Focuses on equitable opportunities in education and employment.
 
• **Karnataka (Article 371-J)**: Provides reservations for the Hyderabad-Karnataka region to address socio-economic disparities.
 
 
 
• **Constitutional Amendments:**
 
 
• Special provisions are created or amended through **constitutional amendments** based on the needs of specific states.
 
• For example, **Article 371-J** was added through the **98th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2012**.
